premises.scope: For every disjoint original-coordinate cross block B in a slab witness of ratio rho, s3(B)<=9sqrt(3e)/rho; stages 1/2 use exact physical conditioning so the projected marginal gates are valid.
Grouped hubs with arbitrary-rank projected crossing remainder; used at (k,ell,d)=(2,1,3), plus exact 3x3 crossing with arbitrary internal functions.
D5: ||p_Q||inf<=5sqrt(2e)e5(M^T M)^(-1/10) for every original-coordinate disjoint cross block, no volume-marginal gate.
For n=3 and all three eigenvalues of modulus>=1, ||p_Q||inf<=6sqrt(pi); numerical no-counterexample search not used as proof.
Supremum equality for nonnegative product kernels between arbitrary cap-one marginals and unit-measure product indicators, without attainment, interval, diameter or fixed-fragment assumptions.
All disjoint/off-diagonal 2x2 minors zero implies A=diagonal+rank<=2; general max-volume skeleton idea noted, dimension-free operator perturbation remains open.

results.statement: For any invertible disjoint physical 2x2 core A[P,Q] and any extra physical column j, W_j=sum_i det A[P+i,Q+j]^2 <=23328 rho^-6. Hence each bordered determinant is <=108sqrt(2)rho^-3. Proof uses reviewed grouped crossing in the diffuse projected one-volume branch and exact physical 3x3 crossing in the heavy-row branch.

Let a=max_{p!=q}|A_pq|. If a>0, after at most four physical hubs the leaf principal block is D+S+E with D diagonal, rank(S)<=4, E symmetric zero-diagonal, bounded physical interpolation coefficients, and ||E||max<=sqrt(108sqrt(2)/(a rho^3)); separately one can ensure ||E||max<=27sqrt(3e)/rho. If a=0 the form is diagonal.
Every disjoint physical cut satisfies e5(A[I,J]^T A[I,J])<=(5sqrt(2e)/rho)^10 and s5(A[I,J])<=5sqrt(2e)/rho.

next_step: Exploit the bounded-coefficient one/two-core skeleton with the reviewed grouped projected-crossing receiver. Route diffuse projected residual energy to a paid k=2,ell=1 crossing and concentrated residual energy to a third physical hub; retain the remaining max-norm twist as a genuine quadratic term rather than deleting it.
